nodes.title: macOS: Expose API to configure native tab bar height in fullscreen collapsed state (`NSTitlebarAccessoryViewController.fullScreenMinHeight`)
Intermittent ERR_FAILED when using CDP.Fetch.requestPaused
nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 41.1.1 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS Tahoe 26.3.1 ### What arch are you using? arm64 (including Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version 40.8.5 ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior Able to pause requests with `CDP.Fetch.requestPaused` and the url is loaded without any errors. ### Actual Behavior When loading a url using `CDP.Fetch.requestPaused`, I receive the following error intermittently: ``` error loading page Error: ERR_FAILED (-2) loading 'http://localhost:1414/' at rejectAndCleanup (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:89325) at WebContents.finishListener (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:89487) at WebContents.emit (node:events:508:28) { errno: -2, code: 'ERR_FAILED', url: 'http://localhost:1414/' } ``` If I add any [WebRequest](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/web-request) listeners then the url always loads correctly. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/46739f4be69d7e07245ba4517334581c ### Additional Information Hello again from the Cypress.io team 👋🏼, I was upgrading to the latest Electron version and noticed this issue. We are currently working around this issue by calling `mainWindow.webContents.session.webRequest.onErrorOccurred(() => {})`.

### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.1.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Tahoe 26.3.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

40.8.5

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Able to pause requests with CDP.Fetch.requestPaused and the url is loaded without any errors.

### Actual Behavior

When loading a url using CDP.Fetch.requestPaused, I receive the following error intermittently:

```
error loading page Error: ERR_FAILED (-2) loading 'http://localhost:1414/'
    at rejectAndCleanup (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:89325)
    at WebContents.finishListener (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:89487)
    at WebContents.emit (node:events:508:28) {
  errno: -2,
  code: 'ERR_FAILED',
  url: 'http://localhost:1414/'
}
```

If I add any [WebRequest](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/web-request) listeners then the url always loads correctly.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/46739f4be69d7e07245ba4517334581c

### Additional Information

Hello from the Cypress.io team 👋🏼, I was upgrading to the latest Electron version and noticed this issue. We are currently working around this issue by calling `mainWindow.webContents.session.webRequest.onErrorOccurred(() => {})`.

nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 41.1.1 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS Tahoe 26.3.1 ### What arch are you using? arm64 (including Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version 40.8.5 ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior The pdf is loaded and doesn't crash. Electron 40.8.5: ### Actual Behavior Electron crashes with: Electron exited with signal SIGTRAP. Electron 41.1.1: ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/mschile/ea93d959bd824fd738b3bff7047526b2 ### Additional Information Hello from the Cypress.io team 👋🏼, I was upgrading to the latest Electron version and noticed this issue. I assume it has to do with the following [breaking change](https://www.electronjs.org/blog/electron-41-0#breaking-changes) in 41: > Breaking Changes Behavior Changed: PDFs no longer create a separate WebContents Previously, PDF resources created a separate guest [WebContents](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/web-contents) for rendering. Now, PDFs are rendered within the same WebContents instead. If you have code to detect PDF resources, use the [frame tree](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/web-frame-main) instead of WebContents. > > Under the hood, Chromium [enabled](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/7239572) a feature that changes PDFs to use out-of-process iframes (OOPIFs) instead of the MimeHandlerViewGuest extension.

nodes.title: Focus broken after closing out of sync showMessageBox in will-prevent-unload
The partial verification scheme for the integrity of asar allows the project owner to modify asar
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

I want to update only the minimal upgrade scheme for asar.
I don't want to disable the asar integrity verification.
I have thought of a plan, but I'm not sure if it can be supported.

### Proposed Solution

Allow configuring a custom private key during construction.
During construction, a public key is generated by combining a custom private key and the hash of asar.
Place the public key externally.
Private key packaged into exe.
When performing Asar integrity verification, it is only necessary to check whether the public and private keys are paired to confirm that the Asar comes from the project itself.



### Alternatives Considered

I don't have a server to use, so I can't consider loading the web.

### Additional Information

The above content was translated using software.

nodes.title: [Feature Request]: Add isolated world discovery APIs to webFrame
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Electron currently has no supported way for preload code to discover or hook into the isolated worlds used by Chrome extension content scripts.

This blocks me from being able to inject `chrome` inside extension content scripts consistently so additional extension APIs can be provided from Electron. Extension pages and service workers can be patched from preload, but content scripts run in separate isolated worlds, and Electron does not expose a supported way to identify those worlds or react when they are created.

Right now, the only possible workaround is to guess world IDs in the reserved extension range starting at `1 << 20` and call `webFrame.executeJavaScriptInIsolatedWorld(worldId, ...)` repeatedly to check whether `chrome.runtime.id` exists. If it does, that world is assumed to belong to an extension content script.

This approach has serious problems:

- It is unsupported and relies on internal world ID allocation details.
- It also create isolated worlds as a side effect of probing them.
- It is timing-sensitive and unreliable across navigations.
- On first load, extension content-script worlds may not exist yet when preload runs, so probing finds nothing.
- On reload, behavior differs: the extension worlds may already exist before preload runs, so the same probing logic appears to work.
- Even when worlds are found later, that is too late for `document_start` content scripts because their top-level code has already executed.

This means there is currently no good way to inject code into extension content-script worlds before those scripts begin running.

### Proposed Solution

A useful solution would be for Electron to expose isolated world discovery and lifecycle APIs to preload, for example:

- `webFrame.getIsolatedWorlds()`
- `webFrame.on('isolated-world-created', ...)`

That would at least allow preload code to discover existing worlds and attach bridges with existing APIs such as `contextBridge.exposeInIsolatedWorld(...)`, without unsafe world-ID probing. The order of the event firing is also very important, as we have to inject code before the content script starts running, otherwise it will be useless.

Relevant existing APIs already assume the caller somehow knows the target world ID:

- `webFrame.executeJavaScriptInIsolatedWorld(...)`
- `webFrame.setIsolatedWorldInfo(...)`
- `contextBridge.exposeInIsolatedWorld(...)`

But there is no way of discovering them.

### Alternatives Considered

**Brute-force World IDs on preload start**

As stated above, looping and probing each world is possible, but it is very unreliable and has inconsistent results based on if the frame just started up or has started before. This would also create new worlds which is very inconvenient, and clog up DevTools Console.

**Delayed scanning / polling**

This is also ineffective as we would discover worlds AFTER they started running, which would mean injecting globals won't have an effect.

### Additional Information

Continuation of #22285
